k: The Drowned Stars
src: 'The Drowned Stars'

k: Ottoline Marsh needs seven Starfall Fragments — splinters of starlight that fell into the Lantern ruins and the Drowned Reef.
src: 'Ottoline Marsh needs seven Starfall Fragments — splinters of starlight that fell into the Lantern ruins and the Drowned Reef.'

k: Look at that sky. Seven little lights where there were none. I'll name one after you. Something dignified. "Wren's Embarrassment."
src: 'Look at that sky. Seven little lights where there were none. I\'ll name one after you. Something dignified. "Wren\'s Embarrassment."'

k: It's still falling, you know. The one that didn't land. The telescope will show you, if you've the nerve.
src: 'It\'s still falling, you know. The one that didn\'t land. The telescope will show you, if you\'ve the nerve.'

k: No starfall yet? Try the old Lanterns. Stars always did like a lighthouse.
src: 'No starfall yet? Try the old Lanterns. Stars always did like a lighthouse.'

k: And something for your trouble. Don't argue. I'm old, I'm allowed.
src: 'And something for your trouble. Don\'t argue. I\'m old, I\'m allowed.'

k: Ottoline sets the last fragment into the great brass orrery. Seven small lights wink on across the dome, and the whole observatory hums like a held note.
src: 'Ottoline sets the last fragment into the great brass orrery. Seven small lights wink on across the dome, and the whole observatory hums like a held note.'

k: There. The drowned stars, back where they belong. Or near enough.
src: 'There. The drowned stars, back where they belong. Or near enough.'

k: You can't put the old sun back, you know. Nobody can. Not the Hierophant, not a hundred Keepers.
src: 'You can\'t put the old sun back, you know. Nobody can. Not the Hierophant, not a hundred Keepers.'

k: But stars are only suns that are very far away. Perhaps the trick isn't to mend the big one. Perhaps it's to make a small one, close by, that belongs to everybody.
src: 'But stars are only suns that are very far away. Perhaps the trick isn\'t to mend the big one. Perhaps it\'s to make a small one, close by, that belongs to everybody.'

k: ...A small one.
src: '...A small one.'

k: It's only a theory. I've written it in the margins of my own book. Nobody reads the margins.
src: 'It\'s only a theory. I\'ve written it in the margins of my own book. Nobody reads the margins.'

k: Now. The thing I wanted to give to the right person. It isn't a thing. It's a way of looking.
src: 'Now. The thing I wanted to give to the right person. It isn\'t a thing. It\'s a way of looking.'

k: Read the sky. Bend fate a little, when it needs bending. Never more than a little. It sulks.
src: 'Read the sky. Bend fate a little, when it needs bending. Never more than a little. It sulks.'

k: ...Oh. Oh, dear. With the chart complete I can see it. One of them didn't land. It's still falling. Toward _us_.
src: '...Oh. Oh, dear. With the chart complete I can see it. One of them didn\'t land. It\'s still falling. Toward _us_.'

k: How fast?
src: 'How fast?'

k: Tonight-ish. Look through the telescope if you're feeling brave. Or foolish. They're the same muscle.
src: 'Tonight-ish. Look through the telescope if you\'re feeling brave. Or foolish. They\'re the same muscle.'

k: Ottoline Marsh finished her map of the drowned stars and taught us to read them. She says you can't mend the old sun — but maybe you can make a small one, close by, that belongs to everybody. I can't stop thinking about it.
src: 'Ottoline Marsh finished her map of the drowned stars and taught us to read them. She says you can\'t mend the old sun — but maybe you can make a small one, close by, that belongs to everybody. I can\'t stop thinking about it.'

k: Through the great glass: seven small lights, and the dark between them, which is not as empty as it looks.
src: 'Through the great glass: seven small lights, and the dark between them, which is not as empty as it looks.'

k: Through the great glass: cloud, cloud, and the faint hum of something very far away. Ottoline's chart has gaps in it.
src: 'Through the great glass: cloud, cloud, and the faint hum of something very far away. Ottoline\'s chart has gaps in it.'

k: Through the great glass: one star, much brighter than the rest, getting brighter.
src: 'Through the great glass: one star, much brighter than the rest, getting brighter.'

k: Keep watching?
src: 'Keep watching?'

k: It is not getting brighter. It is getting _closer_.
src: 'It is not getting brighter. It is getting _closer_.'

k: Well! I'll be updating the chapter on falling stars. It'll be mostly exclamation marks.
src: 'Well! I\'ll be updating the chapter on falling stars. It\'ll be mostly exclamation marks.'

k: Have these spectacles. Mine. They make you notice things. Dreadful habit, noticing.
src: 'Have these spectacles. Mine. They make you notice things. Dreadful habit, noticing.'

k: ...I hate him so much. He sounds like somebody's nice uncle.
src: '...I hate him so much. He sounds like somebody\'s nice uncle.'

k: ...Could not go over.
src: '...Could not go over.'

k: ...I'm not even hungry. That's how you know it's bad.
src: '...I\'m not even hungry. That\'s how you know it\'s bad.'

k: ...Yes. I am.
src: '...Yes. I am.'

k: ...Ugh. Fine. FINE. Don't make that face. I'll get you some wind.
src: '...Ugh. Fine. FINE. Don\'t make that face. I\'ll get you some wind.'

k: ...No. Not this time. Not anymore.
src: '...No. Not this time. Not anymore.'

k: ...I've been told.
src: '...I\'ve been told.'

k: ...OW! Ow ow OW, that STINGS—
src: '...OW! Ow ow OW, that STINGS—'

k: ...Oh. It stopped.
src: '...Oh. It stopped.'

k: ...Yes. I do.
src: '...Yes. I do.'

k: ...I do not have a ribbon.
src: '...I do not have a ribbon.'

k: ...It was hers. The book he gave me. He bought it for her, and she never got to open it.
src: '...It was hers. The book he gave me. He bought it for her, and she never got to open it.'

k: ...Cassian?
src: '...Cassian?'

k: ...I promise.
src: '...I promise.'

k: ...Oh! You look like me! Cass, look, she looks like me, only older—
src: '...Oh! You look like me! Cass, look, she looks like me, only older—'

k: ...I can't. Forgive me. I can't.
src: '...I can\'t. Forgive me. I can\'t.'

k: ...I will choose it every night for the rest of my life. And every night it will be the wrong choice.
src: '...I will choose it every night for the rest of my life. And every night it will be the wrong choice.'

k: ...I know. I know you would.
src: '...I know. I know you would.'

k: ...You're not her.
src: '...You\'re not her.'

k: ...Maybe there was a choice. Maybe Mom had one too, the night Dad went out. And maybe it was this.
src: '...Maybe there was a choice. Maybe Mom had one too, the night Dad went out. And maybe it was this.'

k: ...He's shaking like a leaf. And he hasn't moved an inch.
src: '...He\'s shaking like a leaf. And he hasn\'t moved an inch.'

k: ...This bread?
src: '...This bread?'

k: ...Okay. A little because I owe it.
src: '...Okay. A little because I owe it.'

k: ...He'd hate this. Standing still. He fidgeted. He couldn't sit through a sermon without whittling something.
src: '...He\'d hate this. Standing still. He fidgeted. He couldn\'t sit through a sermon without whittling something.'

k: ...Back in Kiteholm I had twenty kids. I was the oldest. I was ELEVEN. I did the cooking, and the stealing, and the telling-them-it'd-be-fine.
src: '...Back in Kiteholm I had twenty kids. I was the oldest. I was ELEVEN. I did the cooking, and the stealing, and the telling-them-it\'d-be-fine.'

k: ...Just a year's fine. Then thirteen. Then I'll see.
src: '...Just a year\'s fine. Then thirteen. Then I\'ll see.'

k: ...Don't. Don't say it, sparrow. I'll cry, and then Pip'll steal my handkerchief, and then where will I be.
src: '...Don\'t. Don\'t say it, sparrow. I\'ll cry, and then Pip\'ll steal my handkerchief, and then where will I be.'

k: ...He would say that. He always thought it was his fault. It took me years to understand it was our father's.
src: '...He would say that. He always thought it was his fault. It took me years to understand it was our father\'s.'

k: ...Mom?
...Okay. I'll stay.
src: '...Okay. I\'ll stay.'

k: ...There's my girl.
src: '...There\'s my girl.'

k: ...Every good day I ever wanted to keep. All at once. It doesn't want anything else. It never will.
src: '...Every good day I ever wanted to keep. All at once. It doesn\'t want anything else. It never will.'

k: ...We don't put it back.
src: '...We don\'t put it back.'

k: ...She was afraid of the dark.
src: '...She was afraid of the dark.'

k: ...What is your name?
src: '...What is your name?'

k: ...Now she'll know. Now we both will.
src: '...Now she\'ll know. Now we both will.'

k: ...The Afterlight.
src: '...The Afterlight.'

k: ...I want to be a Ranger. And a Cantor. And maybe a baker.
src: '...I want to be a Ranger. And a Cantor. And maybe a baker.'

k: ...Okay, ONE round.
src: '...Okay, ONE round.'

k: ...A quarter of an inch.
src: '...A quarter of an inch.'

k: ...Tomorrow. From Lanternfall.
src: '...Tomorrow. From Lanternfall.'

k: ...I'll come back. The last Halloway who sailed east never came back, I know. But I'm going to. Okay?
src: '...I\'ll come back. The last Halloway who sailed east never came back, I know. But I\'m going to. Okay?'

k: ...Yeah. That's her. Go on, say hello. Mind the edge.
src: '...Yeah. That\'s her. Go on, say hello. Mind the edge.'

k: Forty gold, friend. Opinions are free, the horses aren't.
src: 'Forty gold, friend. Opinions are free, the horses aren\'t.'

k: ...Yeah. Okay.
src: '...Yeah. Okay.'

k: Once more, old man. A girl. Sixteen or so. Black hair. Pale as something pulled out of the sea.
src: 'Once more, old man. A girl. Sixteen or so. Black hair. Pale as something pulled out of the sea.'

k: Pale girls with black hair? Sir, this is a fishing port. Half of us are pale and the other half are bald.
src: 'Pale girls with black hair? Sir, this is a fishing port. Half of us are pale and the other half are bald.'

k: She came ashore on Lanternfall four nights ago. She will try to cross to the mainland. When she does, she comes through here.
src: 'She came ashore on Lanternfall four nights ago. She will try to cross to the mainland. When she does, she comes through here.'

k: The Lord-Commander is not a patient man. I am — but only professionally.
src: 'The Lord-Commander is not a patient man. I am — but only professionally.'

k: Close the shops. Search the inns. Nobody takes the coast road without my leave.
src: 'Close the shops. Search the inns. Nobody takes the coast road without my leave.'

k: ...Black trim on the pauldrons. A sun with a closed eye.
src: '...Black trim on the pauldrons. A sun with a closed eye.'

k: Bram? Those are Dawnguard. Your people. We could just ask them what—
src: 'Bram? Those are Dawnguard. Your people. We could just ask them what—'

k: They're not my people. They're *Thorne's Own*. The Lord-Commander's personal guard.
src: 'They\'re not my people. They\'re *Thorne\'s Own*. The Lord-Commander\'s personal guard.'

k: Psst! You lot. Yes, you, with the very obvious shawl.
src: 'Psst! You lot. Yes, you, with the very obvious shawl.'

k: In. Kitchen door. Now, before the tin-cans come round the corner.
src: 'In. Kitchen door. Now, before the tin-cans come round the corner.'

k: Margarethe Salt. Everybody calls me Mags, except the tax man, who calls me a liar.
src: 'Margarethe Salt. Everybody calls me Mags, except the tax man, who calls me a liar.'

k: I don't know who you are and I don't want to. Down behind the barrels. Not a word.
src: 'I don\'t know who you are and I don\'t want to. Down behind the barrels. Not a word.'
